post_title: A few more features and suggestions.
post_details: Before I get to my "list", I just want to thank all the developers who are working hard on this, I love that we get updates every few months with features and bug fixes I just want you to know I appreciate all the work you do. I understand if some of this stuff might not be technically feasible or fit into the design of the interface or just low on the priority list, but this is just stuff that annoys me when I work. -When you layer clone over/under the sewing around the pattern outline should be (or have the option) divided up into segments rather than one big sewing. - I've previously mentioned this but right now, this is the feature I'd like to see most. -If a sewing line is already selected, and then I click on the start/end point of that sewing line, there shouldn't be a dialog box pop up for an overlapping start/end point. If the sewing line is already selected, I always want to move those start/end points and it's really annoying when it have to manually pick the sewing line I want to adjust. Likewise, I'd like to be able to drag select 2 sewing start/end points and move them together. Also. Linking sewing together manually. I think I've already asked for this, but it's worth repeating. -When you switch a normal map or a texture map or ANY map, it should not reset the transforms on all the other maps. For example, I'll be working and have a normal map that I've resized and then I decide to switch the texture and BAM! the normal map reverts back to the default scale. super annoying. -When you switch fabrics, it should always default back to the "Front" tab. Sometimes I'll switch to another fabric and make a bunch of changes and not realize I'm working working on the backside on the new fabric. -When using the fullness (line) tool- when you curve a portion of a pattern edge, and that edge is already sewn to another edge, I'd love to see the option to have the sewing line divide and scale separately along that segment. This would be extremely helpful when adding gathers to certain areas of fabric. -Fixing the zipper tool/binding/piping- It's really easy. Just give the option to convert these elements back standard fabrics/trim, and not have them be some "special" elements. I really like the idea of combining the process of making a zipper into a single tool, but it HAS to be editable fabric. Also, for the zipper tool, just have it work in the 2d window, with segments. Make it work exactly like the segment sewing/free sewing tools but it creates a zipper. Same with the binding, I love the idea of automating the function but we need the option to convert the binding back to the standard fabric elements. so it would create pattern pieces and fabrics and they would just be part of the pattern, and you could edit them like normal pattern pieces. and again, in the 2d window make it work the same as segment/free sewing. - This one is just a mild annoyance. In the property editor, there is a fabric drop down. This should NOT get triggered by the scroll wheel. So many times I've scrolled down and accidentally changed the fabric this way. Just annoying. Thanks!

post_details: Here are a few things that you can review in your project if your animation is not functioning as desired or expected. PATTERN SETTINGS Lower Particle Distance values causes bouncy garment animations. If you do not need to express detailed creases, it is recommended to set Particle Distance values to either 8-10instead of 5. All garment layers should be set to 0. Sufficient Collision Thickness is required for stable simulation output. If the Collision Thickness value is less than 2, the garments collision detection may not prevent layered garments going through each other during animation. AVATAR SETTINGS Remove or smooth out any rigid geometry such as hair to avoid undesired collision during simulation. Avoid layering garments in areas of the animation prone to collision (bent arms &amp legs). If the garments simulation is too bouncy, increase its avoidance stiffness. d. Select the avatar to access its Property Editor. Increase its Static Friction Coefficient accordingly to determine appropriate value. e. Increase the avatars Kinetic Friction Coefficient to better retain garments styled placement such as the hood draped over the avatars head. MATERIAL PROPERTIES Stretch and Bending values should be less than 60. The garment will drape as if it is in water if the stretch and bending value is larger than 60. Select Fabric in Object Browser to view Physical Properties in Property Editor.
